title: SSO & RBAC Pricing Levers: experimental contract addendum and packaging variants
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Goal: Decide a productized packaging and contract approach for SSO/SAML and tenant-level RBAC commitments for enterprise customers that balances go-to-market velocity, ARR expansion, and legal/sales friction. We will run a 3-arm pricing & contract experiment to observe how different levels of contractual commitment affect conversion, sales cycle length, and downstream support overhead.

Background: Sales consistently asks for guaranteed SSO/SAML support and role-based access controls as part of enterprise deals. Currently SSO is offered as a supported feature on hosted and dedicated plans but enforcement and contractual language vary by deal. This creates ad-hoc concessions and inconsistent pricing. The experiment will produce data to inform whether SSO + RBAC should be: included in a single enterprise SKU, sold as a priced add-on with a signed addendum, or included with standardized security commitments and a price uplift.

Experiment design: Randomized (by net-new qualified trials/accounts) A/B/C test over a 10-week window with target sample ~60 opportunities (min 15 per arm). Variants: 
- Variant A (Control): Status quo. SSO/RBAC available; commitments negotiated case-by-case. No pre-authorized contract language.
- Variant B (Productized Add-On): Offer SSO+RBAC as a clearly priced add-on SKU (list price + implementation fee tier). Minimal contractual language in T&Cs; standard SSO onboarding SLAs.
- Variant C (Committed Addendum): Offer SSO+RBAC bundled into an enterprise plan with a standard addendum that includes: SSO availability SLA (99.9% for auth plane), RBAC scope and support response targets, a filled security questionnaire snapshot, and defined onboarding timelines. Higher list price but reduced negotiation required.

Metrics & success criteria: 
- Primary: % of opportunities that convert to signed contract within 60 days (delta vs control).
- Secondary: median sales cycle length, number of redlines per contract, legal review turn-around time, ARR delta at 12 months, support tickets per customer in first 90 days, and CSAT for security assurance.

Contract language and compliance artifacts: We will ship draft addendum language and a pre-filled security-questionnaire bundle for Variant C. Key clauses being prototyped: authentication availability SLA, responsibility for IdP maintenance, incident communication cadence, RBAC feature commitments (scopes, role templates), data access audit commitments, and limited warranty. Legal feedback so far (LEGAL-112) recommends clauses for escalation and a mechanism for entitlement de-scoping if a customer requires non-standard cryptography.

Rollout plan: 
1) Week 0-1: Finalize pricing bands with Finance. Draft addendum and security snapshot (owner: Legal).
2) Week 2: Sales enablement package and playbooks, demo checklist for SSO onboarding (owner: Solutions Engineering).
3) Week 3-12: Run experiment. Route new qualifying enterprise trials through the randomized variant assignment. Track metrics in Growth dashboard and weekly sync.
4) Week 12-14: Analyze results, synthesize findings, and produce recommendation (include expected revenue and friction trade-offs).

Risks & trade-offs: 
- Sales backlash if price uplift perceived as punitive; mitigated via grandfathering pilot customers and clear ROI messaging.
- Implementation backlog: Engineering/SE capacity to complete SSO onboardings could be a bottleneck (dependency ENG-2481). Mitigation: limit number of Variant B/C seats per week.
- Legal/regulatory concerns for on-prem/air-gapped customers requiring custom crypto; addressed by clause allowing custom addenda at additional cost.

Stakeholders: Sales leadership (revenue targets), Legal (contract language), Solutions Engineering (onboarding), Security & Compliance (noise from questionnaires), Finance (pricing model), Customer Success (support/ticketing).

Deliverables: 
- PM: Experiment plan, pricing bands, recommendation report.
- Legal: Draft addendum and SF-filled security questionnaire.
- Sales: Playbook, price sheets, objection handling.
- Eng/SE: SSO onboarding runbook and limited implementation capacity commitment.

Decision timeline: Final recommendation due by 2026-04-01. If Variant C shows >15% conversion lift with <20% increase in implementation cost and legal turnaround <7 business days, we recommend productizing committed addendum as standard enterprise offering.

Open questions: How to handle Dedicated/VPC customers where KMS/HSM expectations differ? (Engineering to provide matrix for supported environments). What is the acceptable time-to-live for legacy manual concessions (grandfathering timeline)?

release_notes: Experiment will produce recommendation for whether to productize SSO+RBAC as included enterprise SKU or as a standard priced add-on; includes contractual language and a pre-filled security questionnaire for sales use.
